Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A new LEGO set tied to Spider-Man has leaked in advance of its official announcement, and it's based on one of the most iconic moments in the character's history. On an annual basis, LEGO tends to release countless new products that are associated with Spider-Man . While some of these playsets end up being wholly original ideas from LEGO, others are tied to some of Spider-Man's memorable appearances across comic books, movies, and other mediums. To kick off 2027, LEGO is now preparing to drop a new Spider-Man set, and it's perfect for those who grew up watching the original film trilogy.

Coming by way of leaker Unibricks , new details on a LEGO Spider-Man set launching in January 2027 have been unveiled. This set, which is said to be number #67004, is titled "Epic Battle Spider-Man vs. Green Goblin" and is based on the clash between the two characters in the 2002 Spider-Man movie. In particular, this toy recreates the scene on the bridge when Spider-Man has to attempt to save both Mary Jane and a cable car carrying children at the same time.

Although LEGO itself hasn't officially revealed this new Spider-Man set, we have a good idea of what to anticipate from it. The set is said to only boast 240 pieces in total, with its price coming in at a meager $29.99. As for the minifigures that will be included in this release, it's said to come with ones for Spider-Man, Green Goblin, Mary Jane, and a young child who will be able to fit in the cable car.

You can get a look at a mockup of what this new LEGO Spider-Man set should look like right here:

View this post on Instagram For LEGO to be releasing another Spider-Man product based on the original movies isn't a huge surprise given past sets that the toy manufacturer has released. Over the past few years, LEGO has released a set based on the train battle between Doc Ock and Spider-Man from Spider-Man 2 in addition to another tied to the final fight with Sandman, Venom, and Spider-Man in Spider-Man 3 . For the original Spider-Man movie to now be getting some love with a new LEGO release of its own is great to see, even if it's not a shock.

As mentioned, at the time of this writing, LEGO has yet to officially reveal this upcoming Spider-Man playset. Given that it's launching in January, though, this silence surrounding the set shouldn't continue much longer, as its arrival is only a little over a month away. Once it's formally revealed, pre-orders for the Spidey set should soon after go live on LEGO's official website in addition to other retailers.

How do you feel about this new Spider-Man set LEGO is releasing to kick off 2027? And will you be picking this set up for yourself since it happens to be relatively cheap? Let me know all of your own thoughts down in the comments section.

articles.title: Call Me Crazy, But I Don’t Buy Marion’s Gilded Age Twist
articles.summary: Hear me out Gilded Age fans.
articles.content:
Spoilers ahead for the most recent episode of The Gilded Age .

The Gilded Age 's Season 4 premiere had some high stakes drama, and fans went crazy when Marian and Larry had sex after getting caught in a storm. Since then she's been avoiding the Russell boy, but she's now in the midst of a pregnancy scare after suffering from nosebleeds. But is she really with child?

While Marian and her doctor seem to think that she's pregnant due to the chronic nosebleeds, my head went to another place. Namely her job at the settlement house on the Lower East Side. She's been shown tending to ill New Yorkers, so I thought that the pregnancy might be a red herring for her actually contracting something from that gig. After all, she mentioned the settlement house by name multiple times throughout the episode, which was titled "Good Taste."

Marian has been actively avoiding Larry since their tryst, with the Van Rhijn niece harboring a ton of shame and worry about what it could mean for her reputation in New York society. The only thing that could further ruin her chance at marrying well is having a child out of wedlock, which I'm sure would mortify her Aunts, as well as any future suitors.

articles.title: X-Men Fans Will Finally Get THAT Iconic Line in Avengers: Doomsday After Waiting 64 Years
articles.summary: Disney - Marvel James Marsden's Cyclops will finally get to say the X-Men line that was missing from every 20th Century Fox movie for the past 26 years. The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday arrived this morning, and on top of putting Chris Evans' Steve Rogers and his MCU return front and center, it was quick to make […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google James Marsden's Cyclops will finally get to say the X-Men line that was missing from every 20th Century Fox movie for the past 26 years. The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday arrived this morning , and on top of putting Chris Evans' Steve Rogers and his MCU return front and center , it was quick to make it clear to audiences how important the classic X-Men movies are to this new story. Though featuring a team lineup that we've never seen on the big screen before, there's a fidelity in the X-Men's costumes that has long been absent from the screen.

Comic book-accurate costumes aren't the only thing Avengers: Doomsday confirmed today, as it also allowed Cyclops to finally say THE line of the franchise: "To me, my X-Men." Despite countless X-Men movies that have been made over the past three decades, not once has this staple of the comic books been present in the feature films. Though Marvel previously toyed with audiences, expecting an "Avengers assemble," waiting until Avengers: Endgame to actually say it out loud, Marvel Studios just confirmed they're writing a major wrong in Avengers: Doomsday and letting the X-Men have their chance in the spotlight.

In the pages of Marvel comics, "To me, my X-Men" dates back all the way to X-Men #1 in 1963, but arrived in a slightly different form than it is known. Stan Lee and Jack Kirby's original series saw Professor X deliver the line "And now, return to me, my X-Men!" which provided the initial seed for the iconic piece of dialogue.

It wasn't until the '90s that the series really began in the form that we know it now, though it ironically wasn't even said by Professor X himself. 2000s X-Men comics gave Rise to its continued use in the series, though, including in Joss Whedon's Astonishing X-Men when Cyclops himself was given the chance to say the rallying cry.

What's worth noting about the use of the line in the Avengers: Doomsday trailer, though, is not only that Cyclops says the line himself, but who arrives after his call. In the footage, only Nightcrawler, Gambit, and Mystique seem to heed the call of "To me, my X-Men," which could very well indicate some sobering things, like the death of Professor X and Magneto at this point in the film, which would force Cyclops to become the leader (and thus say the line). It may also give us some context for why Cyclops is seen on his knees screaming into the air in the earlier footage from Doomsday .

It's quite surprising that across the thirteen X-Men movies that were made by 20th Century Fox that not once was this line uttered out loud by any character. That said, fans should recall that when these movies were being made, strict adherence to comic book canon was not at all on the mind of the filmmakers when they were creating the movies (as seen in the costumes that the X-Men wore in the original film). Even then, it's wild to think that the X-Men movies made sure to do reshoots and add "I'm the Juggernaut, bitch" to the third film , but never once did anyone say the franchise's signature line.

Poydenis previously was chief revenue officer and co-founder of Influential, a leading creator-marketing company. In joining BuzzFeed, Poydenis is bringing over Jesse Batres, formerly Influential's EVP, head of national sales and partnerships, as president of sales and partnerships. For the third quarter of 2026, BuzzFeed reported total revenue of $26.0 million (down 44%) and net loss of $18.7 million (versus a net loss of $7.4 million the year-earlier period). Allen, in announcing the results, said Q3 was "a transitional quarter."

“The restructuring we announced in July reduced our workforce and dedicated contractors by approximately 35% and we expect this to yield approximately $30 million in annualized savings," Allen said. John Hughes wrote, produced, and directed it, making it part of his series of movies set in a suburb […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Few people would argue that the 1985 film The Breakfast Club isn't a classic. It’s considered one of the best films of the 1980s, and some would go as far as to say of all time. John Hughes wrote, produced, and directed it, making it part of his series of movies set in a suburb outside Chicago. The original film starred Emilio Estevez, Anthony Michael Hall, Judd Nelson, Molly Ringwald, and Ally Sheedy as the titular Breakfast Club, with Paul Gleason cast in the role of the authoritarian vice principal, Mr. Vernon. The film’s main five actors were referred to as the "Brat Pack" by the media and would go on to star in a variety of films throughout the 1980s.

Given how universally beloved of a film it is, it seems almost disrespectful to consider remaking it, even if John Hughes had once considered the idea of a sequel. Hughes died before the idea of the teens serving detention in university came to fruition, and no adaptation or continuation of the film has ever been made. Still, if somebody was brave enough to do a remake of The Breakfast Club, we know who should be cast for it. 

To replace Molly Ringwald, you need star power and a little bit of sass. In The Breakfast Club, Claire Standish strikes the perfect balance between uptight and reasonably guarded, especially in response to John Bender’s overtures. The perfect Claire needs to be able to get called out by the characters for being a “princess” but should nevertheless charm the audience.

There’s nobody who’d be a better fit for that role than Stranger Things and Marvel Cinematic Universe star Sadie Sink. During her tenure as Max Mayfield, Sadie Sink never shied away from a challenge, playing to her full skill set. Max started out as a comedic character, albeit with insecurities and depth, before turning into more of a dramatic powerhouse through her struggles with trauma and Vecna in seasons four and five. Although Sink has only played Jean Grey in Spider-Man: Brand New Day so far, there’s no underselling her performance in the role, and despite the dubious morality of her actions in the film , the audience can’t help but root for her, at least a little bit.

Replacing Ally Sheedy as Allison Reynolds is Geena Meszaros. Meszaros is arguably less known than our other picks for this list, but her performance in Netflix’s The Body is a standout. Meszaros portrayed weird girl Lisbeth Anderson — a character that would likely freak out the so-called weird girl in The Breakfast Club — and embodied a character that viewers loved to hate. Meszaros stole the spotlight in every scene that she was in and possessed an off-kilter magnetism that would be perfect for a role in The Breakfast Club. 

Making The Breakfast Club today also begs the question of how closely to follow the original script, especially with a character like Allison Reynolds. The original film has Claire Standish give her a makeover with makeup to soften Allison’s look, moving her appearance away from her “basket case”. The makeover leads Andrew to express interest in Allison, causing those two to pair up. The connotations around movie makeovers have definitely shifted with time, and it’d be curious to see how a remake of The Breakfast Club would approach the material today.

In 1985, Judd Nelson played John Bender, the so-called delinquent student. Bender spends the majority of The Breakfast Club defying Mr. Vernon and the rules he set for detention, along with antagonizing the other students. After being berated by Mr. Vernon — during which Bender stands frozen still — the audience finds out that Bender and his mother have been physically abused by his father, and Bender’s currently serving detention for pulling the fire alarm. 

Our 2026 pick to replace Judd Nelson is Michael Cimino. Cimino gained popularity as an actor following his lead role in Love, Victor — a loose spin-off of the popular 2018 film Love, Simon — as Victor Salazar, and then a recurring role in the final season of Never Have I Ever as rebellious stoner love interest Ethan Morales. Cimino definitely has the chops to pull off antagonism while concealing a softer underbelly of vulnerability.

Our second Stranger Things star on this list — because, to be real, if we had to call a group of actors in the late 2010s to early 2020s a new version of the Brat Pack, it would be the actors from Stranger Things — Gaten Matazarro would be excellent as Brian Johnson. Matazarro definitely has the nerdy charm and comedic timing needed for Brian. Audiences have seen him play socially awkward for years in his role as Dustin in Stranger Things , and he’s battled academic pressure — and it changed him for the worse — in the 2022 film Honor Society. Really, this feels like a no-brainer.

This was a tough one, and all in all, we may be playing it safe here. In 1985, Andrew Clark was brought to life by Emilio Estevez, even though he was originally cast as John Bender. Estevez was only recast because John Hughes struggled to find the perfect actor for Andrew Clark, and thus the role switched up. As a character, Clark isn’t too much of a stretch from what we’ve seen from Kit Connor before. 

Clark is a jock, influenced both by peer pressure from other jocks and by wanting to gain his father’s approval. Kit Connor rose to fame for his role in Heartstopper as Nick Nelson, the rugby lad with the personality of a golden retriever, and is set to play Cyclops in the MCU. Clark may be rougher around the edges than Nelson, but there’s no reason to believe that Connor wouldn’t do the role justice.

There’s no The Breakfast Club without the authoritarian vice-principal to rebel against — the main adult in the movie, and who, unlike the other characters, has few to no redeeming qualities. He talks down to students, forcefully flaunts authority, and is aggressive to any who stand against him. Whether you agree with his interpretation or not, original actor Paul Gleason saw hidden depths in the character — he felt that when the character read the ending essay, it led him to realize how he’d let the kids down and that he hadn’t understood them at all. Still, for most of the movie, Vernon is that authoritative jerk, even if he might come around at the end. It’s a role somebody has to play.

Our pick for a 2026 Mr. Vernon is Pedro Pascal. Pascal has exuded authority in all of his roles, even if it is usually a lovable one. The one that most immediately comes to mind is his current role as Reed Richards / Mister Fantastic in the MCU . As Reed Richards, Pascal shows he can play a borderline obsessed character, one focused on results and isn’t as skilled with the social aspects of life. There’s a reason Mister Fantastic is worried about being a father, and about the kid turning out like him — he knows that he is the way he hurts other people. A 2026 remake might soften Mr. Vernon through a performance by Pedro Pascal, or it might give the actor a chance to play a truly villainous role.

Disagree with our picks? Would you have cast somebody else? Let us know in the comments below!

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One Piece is now in the midst of the series' biggest fight yet as Luffy and Imu are squaring off in the latest chapters of the series , and now series creator Eiichiro Oda has fully revealed what King Imu actually looks like after all this time. Imu was first introduced to the series nearly a decade ago when it was revealed that there was a mysterious king sitting on a throne at the middle of the world. But this king has made his move much sooner than expected with the climax of the Elbaph Arc.

One Piece: Elbaph Arc has been getting much more intense with each passing chapter , and Imu has revealed his full self now that he's come to Elbaph to make his move against Luffy and the Giants. With the release of One Piece Volume 116 coming to shelves in Japan later this December, the official social media for the series has now revealed its official cover in full and now given fans a full look at what Imu actually looks like. You can check it out below.

One Piece Volume 116 will be hitting shelves in Japan on December 4th, but no international release date has been announced as of this time. It will be collecting Chapters 1180 to 1190 of Eiichiro Oda's original manga series, and that's why it makes a lot of sense that Imu is taking place front and center. His emergence on Elbaph has been the biggest thing to happen in the series over the last few months, and we've only started to see Imu getting even stronger from there.

With Luffy and the others complicating things on Elbaph , Imu arrived on the island as taking it over is going to be very important for whatever plans he might have for the world. While there are still many questions about his origins and the nature of his power, this full devil look for the villain is something that had only emerged once he stepped out of the Holy Land. Which means the black silhouetted figure we had seen before was not just an editorial decision, it was how every other character actually saw the king before.

The latest One Piece chapters have seen Luffy and the others struggling against Imu, but there are some surprising new reveals that have come as a result. It's been confirmed that Imu is on some sort of deadline with how long he can be outside of the holy land as he notes he was reaching his limits, and it seems his presence has had some sort of adverse impact on Luffy's Gear 5 form ( and pushing it to a berserk new kind of level never seen before ). But it's only started to raise more questions.

It's clear that as One Piece 's Final Saga reaches the climax of the Elbaph Arc that the series really is in the midst of its endgame. It's yet to be revealed how many weeks, months or years it make take before Oda actually does end the series, but that grand finale is more real than it ever has been. How are you liking seeing Imu in action with One Piece's latest chapters? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: Colin Farrell: For Emma Fogarty, Who Means the World to Me
articles.summary: I met my friend Emma Fogarty nearly 16 years ago. articles.content:
I met my friend Emma Fogarty nearly 16 years ago. I was sat beside her at a dinner table on an evening purposed to raise awareness for those who have the same punishing condition Emma was born with: epidermolysis bullosa (EB), a rare genetic disorder where the slightest touch or even friction of material rubbing against her skin can cause blistering and open wounds, as the skin struggles to heal. At this stage in her life, Emma’s body is 60-80% open wound. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Late Comedian Sam Kinison — with His AI Avatar — Gears Up for Second Act with Buchwald (EXCLUSIVE)

When she was born, the doctors told her mother and father — Pat and Malachy — that they would be better off leaving her in the hospital as she wouldn’t survive the week. What the doctors failed to diagnose was Emma’s spirit, its beauty, its utter fortitude — and that of her parents, too.

Today Emma is 42, which makes her Ireland’s longest-surviving person with epidermolysis bullosa, and accompanied by constant pain. She lives in fear of cancers, which afflict those with EB in staggering numbers (she is a two-time cancer survivor). But she also lives a life filled with joy, love, meaning and friendship. She has been a wonderful friend to me over these years, providing laughter and support, adventure and her own brand of hard-earned wisdom.

A few years back, I’d mentioned to Emma in passing that we should do a marathon together someday; I’d push her if she fancied. A year after my half-hearted offer, she texted me saying, “Do you remember you mentioned the marathon?” Emma had a dream that I would push her the last 4K of the Dublin City Marathon to mark her 40th birthday, with each kilometer representing a decade of her life that she’d stubbornly refused to let EB dictate. And so… it was on! blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

We decided to chronicle the experience to make the adventure even more special and raise awareness around EB, possibly offering some solidarity to those who live with the pain and cruelty of this condition, including the families whose care is so essential and, at times, heartbreaking. The result is “The Slightest Touch,” a documentary we made together. With the support of Emma’s mom and dad, her sister Catherine, our director Rachel Fleit and many more, what started as a shared dream between us became the shared dream of many; a mini movement of resistance and spirit in the face of unimaginable adversity.

While promoting the documentary, some folks have asked me what it is about Emma or our friendship that makes it so special. I struggle to answer such an honest and simple question because I live inside our friendship and have never objectified it. It’s always been easy with Em. She’s just my dear friend, and it’s a friendship that has deepened through the years. She’s allowed me to be there for her and has shared her trials and triumphs and fears with me. What a great gift. This intensely spirited and brilliant woman has also been there for me. One such example was during the days after my father’s passing.

My siblings and I were sitting by our father’s body during his wake, an open casket in the living room of his former home. The man was a mere husk compared to the vibrant human we’d once known and had complex feelings about. Death simplified our feelings for Dad, but the grief was still profound. As I sat beside his coffin, someone tapped me on the shoulder and said, “Your friend is at the front door.” I stood and saw Emma in her wheelchair making her way into the house with Pat and Malachy beside her.

She hadn’t told me she’d be coming, and it absolutely broke me — but in the way that love can break you only to put you back together again stronger, more whole. And that’s what friends do: they make each other more whole; they offer solace through presence. She didn’t come that day to offer platitudes regarding the realities of loss, or to offer any advice at all. She was just there to be by my side, and to offer my family her company; to acknowledge our grief as we were moving with it and not attempt to assuage it in any way. That day marked what Emma is to me: a true friend, and someone who would be there for me through thick and thin. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I only hope that I can offer her some measure of the same kind of love.

articles.title: People Are Crediting Britney Spears For Black Lace Comeback (But I Think It Goes To Catherine Zeta-Jones)
articles.summary: I must confess, I do believe this.
articles.content:
Britney Spears has made a celebrity fashion statement once or twice in her lifetime, and a recent run of lacy, sheer dresses has been credited to a look she wore back in 2001. While her VMAs dress that year still lands on lists of fans’ favorite fashion looks, I think the look predates this, and credit might actually go to Catherine Zeta Jones, here.

I would never take away any of the wonder around this Spears look. She’s always known how to rock a little black dress , but this is like the holy grail of dresses and it's almost impossible to emulate. I actually think the recent trend of black lace on celebs looks more like a fit Catherine Zeta-Jones once wore, and we can thank her daughter Carys Douglas for reminding us.

Carys Douglas dons her famous mom’s clothing periodically, so when she wore a Gucci top her own mother had worn as part of an ensemble back in 1996 for The Long Kiss Goodnight premiere, it wasn’t a big surprise. Though Zeta-Jones’ original fit included sheer pants, Douglas repurposed the gorgeous top with a skirt for a Gucci event that feels like the silhouette designers have been going for with black lace of late. Take a look.

I really do think the Entrapment actress’ look not only came before Spears’ iconic fashion moment, but it’s also similar to what we’ve seen on younger actresses recently. Gucci also deserves a little bit of credit for being ahead of the curve, and also for putting together some stunning looks, including this one from Dakota Johnson , when the sheer trend came back. Recently, Mckenna Grace wore a similar fit for The Hunger Games . Then Hailee Steinfeld stepped out in a sheer black dress that definitely reminded me of Douglas and her mom.

We’re heading into winter, and we typically see a lot of black after the browns of fall fade out, but I just wanted to give an icon her due where I feel it is due. Though Ms. Spears’ dress is one I will always be thinking about.

Rivaling the Jurassic Park movies in terms of their popularity with young kids, these charming dinosaur movies incorporated various songs and even some pretty harrowing storylines, leading to its enduring status as a classic .

However, it's been a decade since any new Land Before Time movie was released or announced, which seems to suggest the franchise has come to a true end. That hasn't stopped fans from wanting more from these stories and these iconic characters, though, and now, one fan made short film is making that possible in a brand-new 3D format. Specifically, the 3D project Littlefoot , directed by Joey Lever, will be revitalizing this story in a more modern way, all while honoring the original. Check out the trailer for the short film and more about the project below.

The trailer for Littlefoot was released on Nov. 18, marking 38 years since the debut of the original movie. In it, fans of The Land Before Time will find all of their favorite characters, as well as some of the most iconic moments from the entire franchise, from the first time Littlefoot and the "three horn" Cera meet (and she sticks her tongue out at him when her dad says "three horns" don't play with "longnecks") to the devastating loss of Littlefoot's mom, which seems to be a beat for beat recreation of that heartbreaking scene. Along with these are appearances of beloved characters Ducky—including her fan-favorite "yep, yep, yep" catchphrase—Spike, and Petrie.

First trailer for ‘LITTLE FOOT,’ a 3D tribute to ‘The Land Before Time.’ Directed by Joey Lever, the project honors the legacy of the franchise that shaped so many childhoods. pic.twitter.com/Y6JHs7ihZj

So far, fans of the franchise seem overwhelmingly excited about the short film's upcoming release. One commenter under the above video wrote, "That 'Yep yep yep!' At the end broke me," and another saying, "THIS IS SO F—ING CUTE IM GOING TO DIE I LOVED THIS MOVIE SO MUCH OH MY GOD… I need to watch it today so badly holy heck." Still others are talking about how brutally sad some of these scenes are, with one person writing, "My therapist is about to make bank from me after this comes out," and another echoing, "Omg, I teared up just hearing the music." Still others are pleading with the team behind it to make it good, such as one comment reading, "Core memory/trauma unlocked. I have so many memories tied to this movie. Please do it justice."

Notably, many in the comments seem to be confused about what the project is, assuming that it is a full-blown remake headed to theaters rather than a fan-made short film. Either way, there is clearly plenty of excitement, and although the exact release date isn't yet known, it is expected to hit YouTube in 2027.

Were you a fan of The Land Before Time ? Will you be checking out Littlefoot once it is released? Let us know in the comments down below.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Black Clover Season 2 is reaching its final phase as the Spade Kingdom Raid arc is winding down its final battles, and the first look preview for the next episode of the series is setting the stage for Yuno's next big power up. With the first two members of the Dark Triad now defeated , all that stands in the way of the Advent of Qliphoth ritual is Zenon Zogratis. While Yuno and Langris had been able to deal damage to him, the end of the latest episode saw him strike a terrible deal.

Black Clover Season 2 saw Yuno and Langris pretty much defeat Zenon thanks to their teamwork , but the Zogratis sibling saved himself by making a new deal with the Supreme Devil, Beelzebub. Giving himself a devil's heart and new strength as a result, Yuno is now struggling to survive. But the first look images and synopsis for Black Clover Season 2 Episode 9 teases that Yuno is about to unlock a whole new power. Check them out in the gallery below.

Black Clover Season 2 Episode 9 is titled "Yuno Grinberryall" and will be making its debut in Japan on November 28th, and will be streaming exclusively with Crunchyroll when it hits for fans in North America and other international territories. With the latest episode seeing Zenon strike a deal that pretty much puts him on the same level of a Supreme Devil, Yuno and Langris are pretty much out of options. Even with Finral arriving to help, there's still a huge gap in their respective abilities. But the synopsis teases how the scales will balance.

"Yuno, Langris, and Finral are in dire straits under attack from Zenon, who has obtained the heart of a demon," the synopsis begins. "Despite being chosen as the vice-captain of the Golden Dawn, the strongest magic knight squad in the Clover Kingdom, Yuno gnashes his teeth at his inability to protect his comrades, when a grimoire descends upon him." By the sounds of things, Yuno is about to unlock a whole new kind of magic he didn't have before. And it ties to the title of the episode, which fully reveals Yuno's name . We'll have to see what that means for the fight moving forward.

Each new episode of Black Clover Season 2 thus far has been packed to the brim with materials adapted from Yuki Tabata's original manga, and that means these war events have been speeding towards their eventual conclusion. Because while this fight with Zenon is surely going to get a lot of focus, the synopsis also teases other key points in the fight, "Meanwhile, at the site of the Qliphoth's arrival, Dorothy's dream magic is defeated by Morris, who has acquired the power of a demon." But that's not all as the Black Bulls make their move too.

"Just as the gate to the second level of the Underworld is about to open, members of the Black Bulls arrive on their Black Raging Bull to rescue Yami!" the synopsis concludes. The Spade Kingdom Raid arc is quickly reaching its conclusion with the end of this second season, so it remains to be seen what's next for the anime as it readies for the grand finale after . articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Spider-Man is Marvel's most popular character and has been for a very long time. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Spider-Man is Marvel's most popular character and has been for a very long time. If Peter Parker were created across the street at the House of Ideas' distinguished competition, he would have been a sidekick, but Marvel was willing to take a chance with a teen hero as a headliner and it was perfect. The Marvel Universe was already popular but Spider-Man made it even more popular, becoming a household name. The Wall-Crawler wasn't the most powerful hero in the world, but he was tenacious, and that made all the difference. While he couldn't punch it out with the strongest foes out there, he was smart, fast, and skilled, which has allowed him to punch way over his weight class.

Spider-Man pretty routinely faces off against some of the most dangerous villains and skilled heroes out there. More often than not, he wins. That's the thing about Spidey, he often holds back because he doesn't want to hurt anyone, but when he cuts loose, everyone better watch out. Spider-Man is practically Holdsback-Man, but these five formidable Marvel characters still cannot beat him.

Wolverine may not have amazing powers, but let's be real – he's a powerhouse. Wolverine has survived the most brutal battles imaginable and fights at the highest possible level of the superhero community. This is a guy who fights Hulk for fun and even wins sometimes. He's thrown himself at gods and cosmic entities and has been able to not only hold his own, but help get the win. He calls himself the best there is at what he does and he's one hundred percent. Logan has beaten a who's who of the most dangerous fighters out there.

However, one person who he has never been able to get a decisive victory over is Spider-Man. Their early fights saw Spidey win, but just barely, only able to keep a second ahead of the ol'Canucklehead. Since then, as Wolvie has gotten more popular, their fights have gotten closer, with Logan sometimes almost taking down Spidey, but the Wall-Crawler is always able to stay ahead of the mutant berserker. They're best friends now, so they barely fight, but maybe one day Logan will be able to take down Peter.

Colossus is one of the strongest mutants of them all. Piotr Rasputin was born on a Soviet collective farm (although Marvel's sliding timescale probably means that no longer happened), discovering his mutant power to transform into organic steel when saving his sister Illyana from a runaway tractor. He was recruited to the X-Men and soon became the group's heaviest hitter. He's been able to fight it out with foes like Juggernaut and has been able to go toe to toe with the Hulk, Thing, Thor, and Red Hulk. Colossus's strength level is quite high and he's basically indestructible.

However, as tough as Pitor is, he can't beat Peter. In fact, he can't even beat Peter when he has back-up. The first time the two fought was in Marvel Super Heroes Secret Wars, where Spidey whipped the entire team of X-Men by himself. During Avengers vs. X-Men , Spidey volunteered to stay behind to slow down Phoenix Colossus and Magik. He took a hellacious beating, but was able to turn the two of them against each other, leading to them taking each other. Parker almost died and barely landed a punch, but he was still able to beat Colossus, using the mutant's sister as his weapon.

Juggernaut's grudge with his stepbrother Charles Xavier led to him finding the Crimson Gem of Cyttorak and becoming the unstoppable Juggernaut. Marko had always felt inadequate standing next to Charles the genius, so he bullied him, starting an antagonistic relationship that would define the two of them for ages. As Juggernaut, Cain battled the X-Men often, but would eventually become a hired gun alongside Black Tom Cassidy, fighting heroes all over the world as they did their best to make a living as supervillains. Sometimes, Juggs would find himself in New York City and that meant he'd end up tangling with Spider-Man.

Juggernaut is a Hulk-level powerhouse – in fact, he's been able to defeat the Green Goliath several times over the years – but he doesn't have anything on Spidey. The Wall-Crawler is smarter and faster, and has used that to take down his foe. Juggs often leapt before he looked and this tendency allowed Spidey to beat him every time. He once got buried in concrete for months, something that he's never forgotten.

Iron Man is one of the most formidable heroes on the planet. Tony Stark's genius allowed him to grow his family fortune, but eventually his sins would catch up with him, as one of his own munitions injured him. He built the Iron Man chest plate to save his life, and the rest of his armor to escape. Since then, he's been obsessed with making the world a better place, fighting against the greatest threats both on his own and with the Avengers. Iron Man is a icon, one of the leaders of the superhero community, and has worked with Spider-Man many times over the years. However, because this is the Marvel Universe, they've also fought many times as well.

Iron Man is definitely more powerful and better equipped than Spidey, but here's the thing – for most of the last 63 years, the amount of time Peter's been wearing the webs, the Wall-Crawler was more popular than Iron Man. That means that usually Spidey would either win the fight, or it would come out in a draw. I'm sure if Iron Man put his mind to it, he could create something that would allow him to beat Parker, but just because he can build it doesn't mean that he could use it successfully.

The Hulk is the strongest one there is and has been since the day that the Green Door opened. Bruce Banner was a nuclear physicist with the worst possible childhood, and the day of his greatest triumph became the worst day of his life, as young Rick Jones snuck out to the bombing range to honk on his bobo (I swear that is not dirty). Bruce went to save him, the One Below All opened the Green Door, and the Hulk was born. The Green Goliath was empowered with the energy of entropy, gaining infinite strength, invulnerability, and a healing factor, becoming the most powerful human in existence.

The Hulk has basically fought every major (and a lot of minor) characters and has beaten nearly all of them, but Spider-Man has always been able to stay ahead of him. Technically, Spidey has never won one of their fights; he's strong but he can't hurt the Hulk at all. However, he has been able to calm the Jade Giant down or escape him. Basically the best the Hulk has ever gotten out of Spidey is a draw (and no, I'm not counting the recent Infernal Hulk fight; I would have named this entry "Infernal Hulk" if I did).

What other heroes have never been able to beat Spider-Man? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.title: Taylor Swift Was NOT Giving The ‘Peace Sign’ At Travis Kelce’s Game. See Her Celebrating Her DH’s Touchdowns
articles.summary: I was at Arrowhead Stadium, and those two fingers make perfect sense.
articles.content:
I spend a lot of time keeping up with the 2026 TV schedule , but Sunday afternoon I was at Arrowhead Stadium, sitting in Section 107, Row 27, watching Travis Kelce catch two touchdowns against the Arizona Cardinals in person. It was a pretty good day to be a Kansas City Chiefs fan. While I watched Patrick Mahomes and Kelce go to work on the field, a different conversation was brewing online about a familiar hand gesture from the tight end's wife, Taylor Swift . Sorry, Swifties, she wasn’t giving her "peace sign" while celebrating her Dear Husband’s touchdowns.

Now, I didn't have a view into the family suite from my seat. Still, I did watch a woman in front of me continuously use her phone to zoom in and scan the box for, I assume, Taylor. Unfortunately it was to no avail, if her body language was any indication. Thankfully, the broadcast cameras and fans with a clearer vantage point of Taylor dutifully had it covered.

Patrick Mahomes found Kelce for an 8-yard score on the Chiefs' opening possession. Then, late in the second quarter, the quarterback connected with him again on a 22-yard touchdown pass. Kelce finished with six catches for 74 yards as Kansas City beat Arizona 34-7.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday has landed, building anticipation for the upcoming MCU release. The first part of the Multiverse Saga's two-part finale is nearly upon us, with its December 18 release now mere weeks away. The movie is set to tie up various loose ends regarding the MCU's Multiverse story, bringing together a staggering number of Marvel heroes from multiple comic book movie universes on the big screen to battle the all-new threat posed by Doctor Doom. As well as the return of Steve Rogers, the movie's marketing has established Thor as one of its primary heroes. Now, in addition to having him serve as a leader of the MCU's heroes, Avengers: Doomsday seems to be giving Thor a huge power upgrade, as evidenced by the final trailer.

An earlier teaser trailer for Doomsday featuring Thor hinted that the upcoming movie would prove his greatest challenge yet, and the release of the final stage of the film's marketing seems to confirm it. As previously glimpsed in other promotional material, the final trailer showed Thor at the center of a yellow lightning storm, which seems to indicate he will be given a major power upgrade by the Odin Force, which is one of his most powerful forms in the comics. While the trailer naturally keeps any specific details of changes to Thor's powers back, the founding Avenger can be seen seemingly wielding greater powers than MCU fans have ever seen from him on the big screen.

What We Know About Thor's Doomsday Story & What Might Come Next For The Hero As Chris Hemsworth has previously addressed Thor's MCU future , it's difficult to say exactly where the Multiverse Saga's ending will leave the God of Thunder and his MCU story. However, one thing that seems to be clear from the final Doomsday trailer is that the upcoming movie isn't likely to be the end. After showing Thor being easily repelled by Doom while using his familiar powers, the trailer later gives fans a glimpse of what appears to be a huge Thor upgrade. Eagle-eyed Marvel fans have already identified this as potentially the MCU giving Thor access to the Odin Force, so the power boost seems likely to be a key part of Thor's story in Avengers: Doomsday .

However, the trailer's final moments hint at what might come next for Thor, and it's not a development anyone expected. A brief exchange between Thor and Steve Rogers reveals that Rogers will continue to use Mjolnir, with the pair then flying off together. As the scene's place in the movie is impossible to place at this time, it's also plausible that it could simply show Thor and Steve reconnecting before the movie's action gets underway. That said, there appears to be a lack of direct urgency to their exchange, which perhaps hints that the scene might well take place at the end of Doomsday , setting up the duo's involvement in Avengers: Secret Wars .

Should the latter be true, it seems a relatively safe bet that their departure could be to round up reinforcements ahead of the final chapter of the MCU's Multiverse Saga. As Avengers stars missing from Doomsday are thought likely to return for Secret Wars , this notion seems particularly plausible, as it would feature the MCU's longest-standing Avengers setting out to corral more heroes to protect the Multiverse. However, with the sheer amount of unknown elements regarding Doomsday 's plot, it's genuinely impossible to truly fathom what comes next for Thor, even in light of his apparent upgrade in the upcoming Marvel movie.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It seems one long-awaited MCU superhero team may finally be waiting in the wings in Avengers: Doomsday , based on the brand-new final Doomsday trailer —but that also came with the unfortunate confirmation of a major fan fear about the movie. This new trailer includes a host of reveals, from a look at Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter's son and a peek at the movie's X-Men lineup to confirmation that Steve is not actually Loki and Bucky and Steve will finally be reuniting . Yet, these approximately three minutes making up the trailer had even more reveals in store, one of which is the suggestion that one highly anticipated team, that may very well be the future of the franchise, could be coming.

Specifically, audiences already knew that Cassie Lang was going to be in the movie, and there were hints that Kate Bishop would be in Doomsday too. Finally, we have confirmation on the latter, as Kate appears in this final trailer. With both Kate and Cassie accounted for, there is one superhero team in particular that could finally be in the works (arguably, just in time). Unfortunately, though, this exciting reveal also came with a line from Thor that confirms fans were valid in their concerns about Doomsday . Check out the trailer and more about this potential new team and Thor's line below.

The Young Avengers Could Be Coming, But Doomsday Has Another Problem With the appearance of Kate Bishop in the new Doomsday trailer, the possibility that the Young Avengers are on their way in the MCU just got even more likely. For years now, this has been a topic of conversation within the fanbase, and it has long seemed like Marvel is setting up exactly that. So far, it's seemed like slow going, though. Yes, we have Cassie, Kate, Ironheart, the Maximoff twins, Ms. Marvel, and more, but they've largely not come together, and some of these characters seem to have been altogether sidelined. However, the MCU is said to be getting a soft reboot after Avengers: Secret Wars , which may be the perfect time for the Young Avengers to step in. Perhaps this is what Kate and Cassie's appearance in Doomsday will kick off.

While that is exciting, this trailer does introduce another problem—or, rather, it confirms what fans had long been worried about. Specifically, Thor at one point makes a comment about not knowing half of the heroes he is fighting alongside. This was an issue fans raised months ago, with memes about Doomsday mostly being character introductions making the rounds online for quite some time. It's unlikely that there will really be that many drawn out character introductions, but it does suggest that this Avengers team-up may not be as satisfying or meaningful as what happens in Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame . Of course, it's possible that Doomsday will still make it work somehow, and the wait to find out is nearly over, as Doomsday hits theaters in less than one month, on Dec. 18.

articles.content:
ITV has said its duty of care to I'm A Celebrity… Get Me Out Of Here! contestants is of the "utmost importance" amid concern over an incident between campmates AJ Odudu and Mariella Frostrup .

On Sunday evening, ITV broadcast footage of tensions between Big Brother host Odudu and broadcaster Frostrup over camp cooking duties (see below).

During one exchange, Frostrup accused Odudu of being "aggressive" and creating a "drama out of a crisis." Odudu implored Frostrup not to "use those words towards me," adding: "'Dramatic' and 'aggressive' are very harsh words." The duo attempted to hash it out in a later conversation, during which Frostrup apologized. "Please don't call me aggressive," Odudu asked. "Only if you're not being aggressive," Frostrup replied. "So you stand by that?" Odudu added. articles.title: N64 Series Dormant Since 2008 May Finally Be Returning
articles.summary: A series that got its start exclusively on the N64, which has been dormant since 2008, may finally be returning after nearly two decades. The series in question specifically dates back to 1998, and it was once a Nintendo series made exclusively for its console. At the time, this console was the N64. That said, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A series that got its start exclusively on the N64 , which has been dormant since 2008, may finally be returning after nearly two decades. The series in question specifically dates back to 1998, and it was once a Nintendo series made exclusively for its console. At the time, this console was the N64. That said, Nintendo no longer owns the series. Now, Xbox owns the series, and Xbox has given it to Activision to manage, with Activision being the publisher primarily known for the Call of Duty series.

Over on LinkedIn , alongside Call of Duty , Crash Bandicoot , Spyro the Dragon , Halo , Sea of Thieves , and Age of Empires , Activision lists Banjo-Kazooie as one of its iconic gaming franchises. Banjo-Kazooie sticks out in this list, as every other game in this list is either active or semi-active. It's the only dormant one, unless it's not staying dormant.

"Activision is home to iconic gaming franchises including Call of Duty , Crash Bandicoot , Spyro the Dragon, and now… Halo , Age of Empires , Sea of Thieves , and Banjo-Kazooie ."

Now calling Sea of Thieves iconic or even Age of Empires iconic feels like a stretch. Mario is iconic. The former is a popular game, and the latter is an important legacy series, but they aren't iconic. The same applies to Banjo-Kazooie as well. This is only relevant because it may be wise not to make too much of this list, as it may just be simple PR jargon and nothing more. It would be odd to reference a very dormant series in this way if you didn't have plans for it, but certainly plausible, especially when the reference is in a very generic PR statement.

Just this year, Xbox publicly responded to demand for the series to return . It didn't announce anything or make any commitments, but a response itself is noteworthy compared to no response. Meanwhile, just this month, a few games in the series were made free to all Xbox Game Pass subscribers .

As for the series itself, for those unfamiliar with it, it debuted in 1998 via the N64 and developer Rare. This first game was obviously called Banjo-Kazooie . In 2000, a sequel followed called Banjo-Tooie . This was another N64 exclusive. Then in 2003, there was Banjo-Kazooie: Grunty's Revenge for the Game Boy Advance, but while this one was also made by Rare, it was published by THQ after Microsoft acquired Rare from Nintendo. In 2005, there was another Game Boy Advance installment, Banjo-Pilot , from the same pair. Then came the final game in the series, and the first published by Xbox since Xbox acquired Rare and the IP from Nintendo. This game was Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts & Bolts , an Xbox 360 exclusive. Since then, the series has been on ice.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Rockstar Games has begun releasing the first big update for Grand Theft Auto 6 following its launch. Prior to its arrival this past week, Rockstar let loose a couple of pre-release patches for GTA 6 . Since the game wasn't yet live, players weren't sure what these updates actually did, but they were likely meant to polish GTA 6 just a bit more and resolve any last-minute issues that those at Rockstar may have found. Now, with players having spent time with GTA 6 for roughly four days, Rockstar has started to implement new fixes based on errors that have popped up frequently.

As of today, Grand Theft Auto 6 update version 1.002.002 has started to roll out across PS5 and Xbox Series X/S platforms. The patch isn't an enormous one by any means, as it mainly looks to address random bugs players have been running into. By far the biggest issue that Rockstar has resolved is related to autosaves, as this feature wasn't working as intended for some players. As a result, some lost quite a bit of progress when playing GTA 6 due to the autosave function not operating as it should.

The remainder of the bugs that Rockstar has fixed in this update are much less notable, for the most part. Some of these errors are related to game crashing, while others are tied to Wanted Levels and phone calls not working properly. Moving forward, Rockstar will undoubtedly continue to release more updates for GTA 6 like this, some of which will surely end up being far more extensive. For the time being, though, it's great to see how quickly Rockstar has responded to complaints that some players have had and has looked to rectify these issues sooner rather than later.

UTA is moving to a new London HQ alongside Curtis Brown and soccer agency ROOF for the first time.

The agency is bringing all of its London businesses together in a 70,000 square foot HQ in New Rathbone Square, which is round the corner from its current Newman Street HQ, where it has been for three years . Curtis Brown is also close by in Regent Street, while staffers from Munich-headquartered ROOF's London hub have been in Newman Street for a few months.

Keith Scholey and Alastair Fothergill are stepping back from the day-to-day running of Our Planet maker Silverback Films after 14 years.

The pair of storied natural history makers will be replaced by a new team following a revamp at Silverback, which is now owned by Banijay .

Jane Hamlin , currently Chief Operating Officer, will become Chief Executive Officer; Executive Producer Huw Cordey will take on the role of Chief Creative Officer; and Deputy Director of Production Elly Salisbury will become Chief Operating Officer. After a lengthy spell at BBC Studios, Scholey and Fothergill founded Silverback in 2012. Upcoming are Dolphins: My Close Encounters , premiering on Netflix on December 28, and Disneynature's Wolf , arriving on Disney+ in April next year.

Silverback said the transition will see the outfit work more closely with Banijay UK, which was merged with Silverback's previous owner, All3Media , a few weeks ago. articles.title: 'The Odyssey' Star Samantha Morton Honored With BFI Fellowship

articles.content:
The Odyssey star Samantha Morton is set to receive the British Film Institute's highest honor, the BFI Fellowship.

The award recognizes the actress for her "extraordinary talent for bringing empathetic, raw and complex performances to her work," such as in indie films Under the Skin , Morvern Callar , Control and Synecdoche, New York , major international blockbusters such as Minority Report and TV hits such as The Walking Dead .

Most recently, the Academy Award nominee and Golden Globe winner was a scene-stealing presence as Circe in Christopher Nolan's box office behemoth The Odyssey , skyrocketing to the forefront of the awards conversation. She'll pick up the BFI Fellowship at the BFI Chair's dinner at London's The Rosewood on Jan. 28, hosted by BFI chair Jay Hunt. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Business UTA to Unite Businesses at New London Headquarters in 2027 Movies Finally, the U.K. Can See Everything: Nathan Fielder's Elizabeth Holmes Doc Makes British Box Office History

Morton said the honor is the greatest gift she could imagine, and spoke about platforming working-class talent. "To be welcomed into such a distinguished community means the world to me," she began on Monday. "Both historically and moving into the future, to have female working-class voices amongst past esteemed recipients means I can reach and hopefully teach and inspire a whole new generation who may be unfamiliar with the opportunities waiting for them. "I accept this honour," she added, "and assume this role with the gravity it deserves… From my first serious film role in Carine Adler's Under the Skin to bringing Circe to life for Christopher Nolan in The Odyssey , a truly life=changing experience, the BFI has always been there, a guardian of my hopes as an artist. articles.title: 'The Dinosaurs,' 'Ocean With David Attenborough' Producer Silverback Films Gets New Top Execs
articles.summary: The Banijay natural history banner says founders Keith Scholey and Alastair Fothergill will leave day-to-day management to CEO Jane Hamlin, creative chief Huw Cordey and COO Elly Salisbury.
articles.content:
Banijay 's natural history producer Silverback Films ( Ocean With David Attenborough ) has unveiled a new leadership structure, promoting three senior executives from within, with founders Keith Scholey and Alastair Fothergill shifting their focus from the day-to-day management of the company to the positions of executive chairs. In their new roles, the two will concentrate on creative development and production of new films and series.

Current chief operating officer Jane Hamlin will become CEO, executive producer Huw Cordey will take on the role of chief creative officer, and deputy director of production Elly Salisbury will become chief operating officer (COO). The changes will take effect on Jan. 1, 2027. Fothergill will focus on landmark natural history series, building on his work as executive producer of Our Planet , Wild Isles and Life on Our Planet . Scholey will continue to work on feature documentaries, following the success of David Attenborough: A Life on Our Planet and Ocean With David Attenborough . Founded in Bristol in 2012, Silverback has grown from a small team into a company with longstanding relationships with the BBC, Netflix, National Geographic and Disney. articles.title: How I Would Change The Survivor Coin Flip To Solve The Runtime Problem
articles.summary: Hear me out Survivor fans.
articles.content:
Spoilers ahead for the most recent episode of Survivor .

MrBeast introduced the coin flip in Season 50 , changing how much money Survivor contestants make. Last season Rick Devens successfully called it a doubled the prize pot, but poor Lewis Kelly was eliminated after his attempt this season. Unfortunately this scene wasn't all that thrilling to watch, as anyone who was watching live knew that there wasn't enough time in the episode for the contestants to vote and for host Jeff Probst to read them out. So what's the solution here?

You might be thinking, but what if the person who successfully flips the coin was the target of the votes? This is definitely a possibility, but I think their immunity would work the same as if they had used a Hidden Immunity Idol. Those votes won't count, and the person with the second-most votes would be the one who gets eliminated from the game. Sure, the Survivor contestants will have to commit to their vote before finding out if the coin flip was successful, but I think that only adds a unique strategic challenge to the situation.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Marvel star Charlie Cox is known by audiences around the world as Daredevil in the MCU, but he also claims he was interested in playing another iconic movie character: James Bond . Now that Robert Pattinson has officially been cast as James Bond , speculation over who will take over the role after Daniel Craig's departure has finally ceased. For five years, fans have heard rumors of many potential new Bonds, with some names proving far more popular choices than others. As the quintessential movie spy as well as a charming action hero, getting the perfect actor to play James Bond is absolutely crucial for the continued success of the franchise. While Pattinson's casting is a strong choice, many will now lament that Charlie Cox was told he was too old to play the iconic spy.

While speaking with Virgin Radio UK, Charlie Cox revealed that when he asked to audition for the role of James Bond, he was rejected with reasoning that now feels a little hypocritical. As reported by DiscussingFilm on X , Cox claims he was told that he was too old for Bond, and explained that he and Pattinson are not too far apart in age. As Cox prepares to turn 44, the announcement of the 40-year-old Robert Pattinson as the next Bond is sure to make that reason for his rejection sting a little. There are a few explanations as to why Cox's interest in playing James Bond may have been so readily dismissed, though none are likely to soften the blow for fans who believe he'd have been a perfect fit for the role.

Looking back at the ages of each new Bond in their respective debuts, it's a little baffling that Cox wasn't even given the chance to audition for the role. However, considering the search for the next James Bond will have prioritized certain qualities over others, it's not entirely unsurprising that even a major actor like Cox would be rejected out of hand. While Cox's stint as Daredevil has earned him a huge amount of popularity due to its mix of dramatic emotional scenes and brutal, hard-hitting action, the subtext of Bond as a character is considerably different. Also, just because we can see the many ways Cox would clearly fit the role of 007, that doesn't mean he's what director Denis Villeneuve or the franchise's producers had in mind for the next Bond.

Of course, one of the most important qualifying factors for any prospective Bond is their ability to convincingly play a British spy, and that's a box that Cox conveniently checks. However, as ideas about the character have repeatedly evolved and varied over the years, the particular vision that the creatives involved with selecting Daniel Craig's successor originally had might not match up at all with Cox's talents. Additionally, they may have initially been seeking a younger actor to bring a more youthful take on the character to life — reports suggest Harry Styles was even considered for the next James Bond — but this criteria may have been reconsidered since Cox's rejection.

Hollywood history is filled with near-misses and what ifs, and the role of James Bond is no different. Many major stars have been rumored or connected to the coveted role, but for a variety of reasons, these castings never came to pass. The one thing that's certain is that Charlie Cox is another name to add to this list, and perhaps the biggest thing we can glean from his reported rejection is just how delicate a task casting the next Bond must be. Undoubtedly, the process required a massive amount of consideration, with certain ideas likely to have been disregarded or adopted along the way. The process of casting a role as high-profile as Bond was always going to be a complicated one, and while we'd have loved to see Charlie Cox in the role, Robert Pattinson is also sure to be an exciting addition to the exclusive ranks of cinematic 007 actors.

Do you think Charlie Cox would have made a good Bond, or is Robert Pattinson a better fit? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

In addition to that, this latest trailer confirms that these groups will be coming together in one massive team-up—with Thor, sadly, acknowledging that he doesn't know half of them, thereby making one fan concern true. Along with the scenes showing those team-ups, however, was a shot at one highly-anticipated character reunion, and it will hopefully mean the MCU finally resolving a major problem left in the wake of Avengers: Endgame . Check out the trailer and more about this character reunion below.

Steve and Bucky Will Reunite in Doomsday Image courtesy of Marvel Studios The end of Avengers: Endgame left a massive question mark in regards to Bucky and Steve's relationship—one that infuriated fans and that the added scenes in Avengers: Endgame Encore didn't clear up. Namely, with Steve deciding to stay in the past and then returning as an old man towards the end of the movie, the implication was that Steve had lived out his days in the past as a happily married man, not as a superhero. This led to outrage and backlash from fans, as that would mean that Steve had a sweet little domestic life all while he knew his best friend was out there being tortured by Hydra. What's more, Steve had clearly left Bucky to fend for himself following Endgame (which audiences have now seen play out on screen in multiple projects).

While that narrative may still be true for the most part, the Doomsday trailer has, at least, confirmed that Bucky and Steve come back together again. In a blink-and-you-miss-it moment, the two embrace in the final trailer, setting up a reunion that fans have waited literal years for. Now, it just remains to be seen whether the two address the elephant in the room, which is Steve's decision not to return to the present time, as they had all seemingly agreed upon before he went to return the Infinity Stones. It's not clear at this point whether Bucky is as hurt by Steve's choice as fans were (although it's difficult to imagine he is, based on the extent of the outrage), but hopefully, they will at least address it.

However, this also raises some interesting questions about Steve's eventual fate. Namely, how could he return as a happy old man at the end of Endgame , especially with a ring on his finger, the story about which Sam doesn't know, given what we see in these trailers? In less than one month, fans will finally know.

What do you want to see from Steve and Bucky's reunion? Let us know in the comments down below.

articles.title: 5 Psychological Horror Movies That Show Why We Love Being Scared, Including a Stephen King Film He Hated
articles.summary: There's something curious about watching horror movies, after all, why do we enjoy stories that scare us, build tension, or make us uncomfortable, even when we know everything is going to end terribly for the characters? A lot of the answer can actually be found in horror movies that don't follow the genre's more traditional […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There's something curious about watching horror movies, after all, why do we enjoy stories that scare us, build tension, or make us uncomfortable , even when we know everything is going to end terribly for the characters? A lot of the answer can actually be found in horror movies that don't follow the genre's more traditional formulas, such as slashers and monster stories . Ever heard of psychological horror? These are the kind of films that leave us uneasy about something that's either difficult to explain or so deeply rooted in human experiences that it gets under our skin on a personal level.

If you enjoy psychological horror, this list features some of the best examples of how this genre can explain, in its own way, why we love feeling disturbed and terrified.

What The Babadook does best is make you feel afraid of something that goes beyond finding a monster inside your own home (which is already pretty terrifying on its own). In fact, this movie is more concerned with the feelings its protagonist tries to hide than with the creature itself. The story follows Amelia (Essie Davis), a widowed mother who's exhausted from trying to raise her son, Samuel (Noah Wiseman), a difficult child who still hasn't come to terms with his father's death. And when the two come across a children's book about a frightening creature called the Babadook , Samuel's behavior becomes a little more concerning, while Amelia also notices strange things happening around her.

The psychological suspense works because, as things get worse, it's difficult to separate the supernatural from Amelia's emotional struggles. She's not a mother who knows how to handle every challenge; she's tired, frustrated, and has a hard time showing affection toward her own son. So, when Babadook enters the picture, it brings all those feelings to the surface, including the ones many people would rather not admit they have. And this approach does a great job of explaining our fascination with fear because, deep down, the movie is dealing with very real problems. The Babadook is frightening in its own right , but its message also touches on something personal. The difference is that, because we're watching it unfold on screen, we don't have to deal with the consequences ourselves, which allows us to enjoy it.

Considered by many to be the best horror movie of the century , Get Out has more than enough reason to be on this list. Its premise is pretty effective since it takes a situation most people would already find uncomfortable and turns it into a nightmare. The story follows Chris (Daniel Kaluuya) , a Black photographer who travels with his white girlfriend, Rose (Allison Williams), to spend a few days at her family's estate. At first, her parents seem friendly, even if they make some awkward comments and show a few strange behaviors. But Chris soon realizes that something is wrong not only with them, but also with the Black employees working on the property. And the social commentary here is so powerful that the way Jordan Peele handles it is a masterclass in filmmaking.

Chris is surrounded by people who say they're not racist, but whose actions show that's not exactly the case. Horror becomes a way to explore the objectification of Black people and racism disguised as admiration. The Sunken Place sequence, for example, is amazing because it turns the feeling of not being heard or having no control over your own situation into a literal experience—it's surreal. And as you follow Chris trying to figure out what's going on, you also see that he's in a position where fighting back could make things worse. Overall, it's about the fear of being judged, manipulated, or put in danger by those who pretend to be something they're not . And it's even scarier when you remember that Get Out deals with a reality many people actually experience.

Maybe you've felt this way yourself, or you know someone who believes they need to be perfect to have any worth. Well, Black Swan explores this idea so well that you'll find yourself disturbed as you watch what someone is willing to do to reach the top. The movie introduces us to Nina Sayers (Natalie Portman), a ballerina who lands the lead role in a production of Swan Lake, where she has to portray both the White Swan and the Black Swan. The problem is that she's perfectly suited to the character's delicate and disciplined side, but struggles to show the sensuality and spontaneity required for the other role. Soon, she's dealing with pressure from the director, competition with a new dancer, and also a controlling mother.

So you watch all of this, following a protagonist who can't separate her personal identity from what she does professionally, making any sign that someone else might be better than her feel like the worst threat ever. Black Swan even adds elements of body horror to help you understand what it's like to be consumed by an obsession, and it does brilliantly. But more importantly, as suggested earlier, this is a story people can relate to because it deals with familiar situations like the pressure to deliver results, comparing yourself to others, and always feeling like you're not doing enough. And by taking these everyday struggles to extreme levels, you get curious to see just how far Nina will go.

Rosemary's Baby is one of the classics of psychological horror , and this reputation comes from exploring something that can naturally make us feel vulnerable: helplessness. Rosemary Woodhouse (Mia Farrow) is a woman who moves into an apartment in New York with her husband, Guy (John Cassavetes), and becomes pregnant shortly afterward. At first, the couple's life seems to be going just fine, but then their elderly neighbors start getting a little too close, and people around Rosemary begin acting strangely—something only she seems to notice. So, she realizes that something is going on, but her husband and even the doctors keep trying to convince her that everything is fine. Ultimately, you watch someone being pushed closer to the edge because nobody is willing to listen.

And that's without even getting into the pregnancy, because Rosemary isn't just worried about her own safety, but also about what might be happening to her child. The movie does a great job of exploring this feeling of helplessness, especially by showing how the choices being made about her own body aren't really hers to make. Rosemary's Baby is specifically a story about Satanism and conspiracy , but it's also about manipulation and control. And even after all these decades, this approach still works, as it makes you just as paranoid and suspicious of everyone as the main character. In other words, the movie succeeds at making the audience experience the effects of psychological horror, and you keep watching because you need to know how everything will turn out, even when you have a feeling it's not going to end well.

Stephen King is the king of horror stories, and many of his books have already been adapted over the years . And one of them, despite being quite different from the source material ( something that bothered the author ), is still a great example of how to mess with an audience's mind. The Shining centers on Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson), a writer who accepts a job as the winter caretaker of the Overlook Hotel, bringing his wife, Wendy (Shelley Duvall), and his son, Danny (Danny Lloyd), with him. The idea is to take advantage of the isolation to work on his book, but the supernatural presence inside the hotel starts affecting the family, mostly Jack. His transformation doesn't take long, but it's still terrifying to watch (especially thanks to Nicholson's performance).

This is a character who becomes a threat to his own family, and even though the hotel and its occurrences are important, the possibility of a father losing control is what gives the story its weight. Besides, The Shining has many scenes that emphasize isolation, endless hallways, and some kind of oppressive atmosphere— some sublime direction from Stanley Kubrick . So, as you watch, you get the feeling that there's something seriously weird with the place (and in the worst way possible). Basically, the movie combines the fear of the unknown with the experience of living with someone familiar whom you can no longer recognize. And what's fascinating is that you can never really explain how or why everything happens the way it does.

articles.title: 'Avengers: Doomsday' Final Trailer Shows Major X-Men Moment
articles.summary: The final trailer for the Marvel superhero mashup is the best look yet at the upcoming blockbuster.
articles.content:
The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday is here.

In perhaps the best look yet at the upcoming Marvel superhero mashup (below), the footage is largely focused on Captain America (Chris Evans) and his return from domestic bliss with Peggy Carter (Hayley Atwell) into trying to save the world once again.

There's also some new footage of Doctor Doom (Robert Downey Jr.) as he tells the heroes, "All of you have lived stolen lives, now you must give them back."

While Thor (Chris Hemsworth) is urging the heroes to "put aside your petty squabbles" while admitting, "I don't even know who half of you are." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies Bassam Tariq Says Marvel's Scrapped 'Blade' Reboot Taught Him "Life's Too Short to Make Sh** Films" Hollywood Flashback When Kevin Feige Got Off to a Less-Than-Incredible Start at Marvel

But the moment fans are buzzing about most has Cyclops (James Marsden) assembling the X-Men — in a scene that recalls the famous circle-up shot in 2012's The Avengers — and declaring, "To me, my X-Men."

The film from directors Joe Russo and Anthony Russo is set to hit theaters Dec. 18.

The film has a sprawling cast, ranging from stars of the original 2000s X-Men movies such as Patrick Stewart and Ian McKellen, to Black Panther ‘s Letitia Wright and Winston Duke, to more recent MCU additions, such as Shang-Chi ‘s Simu Liu and Fantastic Four: First Steps ‘ Pedro Pascal, Vanessa Kirby, Ebon Moss-Bachrach and Joseph Quinn.

There’s also Captain America actor Anthony Mackie and Ant-Man star Paul Rudd, in addition to Thunderbolts players Sebastian Stan, Florence Pugh, Wyatt Russell and David Harbour.
